questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to this project's CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: main branch, reviewing the User Dashboard Page plan.
ELI10: gstack can add a short "Skill routing" section to CLAUDE.md so future sessions automatically pick the right skill (e.g. design review, QA). Without it, you invoke skills by name yourself.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Either an unwanted CLAUDE.md edit + commit, or future sessions don't auto-route to skills.
Recommendation: A because it is one-time and makes skill selection automatic.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Note: plan mode is active, so if you pick A the CLAUDE.md edit + commit is deferred until after plan mode ends; nothing is written now.
Pros / cons:
A) Add routing rules (recommended)
  ✅ Future sessions route requests to matching skills without you naming them
  ✅ One-time setup, a small appended section at the end of CLAUDE.md
  ❌ Edits and commits CLAUDE.md, which in this repo is a fixture file
B) No thanks
  ✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as it is, no commit is created
  ✅ You keep full manual control over which skill runs
  ❌ You must invoke skills by name every time going forward
Net: automatic routing versus leaving CLAUDE.md untouched.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description: Append the Skill routing section to CLAUDE.md and commit (deferred until plan mode ends).

questions.question:
D2 — Review focus for the User Dashboard plan
Project/branch/task: main, design review of the User Dashboard Page plan (review-input.md).
ELI10: I rated this plan 4/10 on design completeness. The biggest gaps are page hierarchy per breakpoint, what each activity/notification row actually shows, and the real copy/behavior for empty, error, modal and toast states. Next I generate visual mockups, then walk all 7 design dimensions. You can narrow that.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Narrowing skips dimensions, so an unreviewed gap (e.g. accessibility or responsive) ships as whatever the implementer guesses.
Recommendation: A because the plan has gaps in nearly every dimension, so a narrow pass would leave known holes.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10
Pros / cons:
A) All 7 dimensions (recommended)
  ✅ Every dimension gets rated and every gap gets its own decision
  ✅ Hierarchy, states, a11y and responsive all land in the plan before code
  ❌ More questions to answer, one per gap (human: ~1 hr / CC: ~15 min)
B) Focus on specific areas only
  ✅ Fewer questions, faster to a revised plan for the areas you care about
  ✅ Lets you skip dimensions you already have opinions on
  ❌ Unreviewed dimensions stay at their current low scores in the report
Net: full coverage versus fewer questions.

options.label: All 7 dimensions (recommended)
options.description: Mockups first, then full 7-pass review with per-gap decisions.

options.label: Specific areas only
options.description: Tell me which dimensions (e.g. hierarchy, states, a11y) to focus on.

questions.question:
Want outside design voices before the detailed review?
D3 — Outside design voices
Project/branch/task: main, User Dashboard Page plan design review.
ELI10: Before the 7 passes, I can get second opinions: Codex scores the plan against hard design rules and litmus checks, and a separate Claude agent does an independent completeness read. It costs a few minutes and gives a cross-check.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Skipping means one reviewer's judgment; running costs time and Codex may be unavailable.
Recommendation: B because the plan's gaps are already concrete and a single native pass covers them; this is a taste call.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: a cross-model check versus a faster path to the fixed plan.

options.label: Yes, run outside design voices
options.description: ✅ Codex hard-rule + litmus scorecard plus an independent Claude completeness read. ✅ Disagreements surface with both perspectives in the relevant pass. ❌ Adds a few minutes; Codex may be missing here, in which case only the Claude voice runs and it's tagged single-model.

options.label: No, proceed without (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Straight into the 7 passes with the approved mockup as anchor. ✅ Fewest steps to a fixed plan. ❌ Findings rest on one reviewer; no cross-model check on slop risk or hierarchy.

questions.question:
D4 — Search learnings across your other projects?
Project/branch/task: main, User Dashboard plan design review.
ELI10: gstack keeps local notes ("learnings") from past sessions. It can search notes from your other projects on this machine too, which helps when patterns repeat. Nothing leaves your machine.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Cross-project on can mix in patterns from unrelated client codebases; off misses reusable lessons.
Recommendation: A because for a solo developer reusable lessons outweigh cross-contamination risk.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Enable cross-project learnings (recommended)
  ✅ Past lessons from other repos on this machine can inform this review
  ✅ Stays fully local, one-time setting stored in gstack config
  ❌ Patterns from unrelated client projects could leak into recommendations
B) Project-scoped only
  ✅ Each project's learnings stay isolated, no cross-client contamination
  ✅ Simpler mental model of where advice comes from
  ❌ Misses lessons already learned elsewhere on this machine
Net: broader recall versus strict per-project isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description: Set cross_project_learnings=true and search across local projects.

questions.question:
D5 — Issue 1: Which content leads the dashboard, and how do panels lay out?
Project/branch/task: main, User Dashboard plan, Pass 1 Information Architecture.
ELI10: The plan names three panels but never says which one the user sees first. Without that, the engineer picks an order (usually the order in the spec) and every panel gets equal weight, so nothing stands out. Unread notifications are the only thing here that asks the user to do something, so they should win.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Users landing after login scan an undifferentiated grid and miss unread items, or the page is rebuilt after launch.
Recommendation: 1A because notifications are the only actionable content and "hierarchy as service" says the actionable thing goes first.
Completeness: 1A=9/10, 1B=8/10, 1C=5/10
Pros / cons:
1A) Notifications primary, Activity secondary (recommended)
  ✅ Unread items are the first thing seen on every viewport, matching the user's real job
  ✅ lg: two columns (Notifications 7/12 left, Activity 5/12 right); base/sm/md: single column Notifications then Activity
  ❌ Activity gets less width on desktop, so long activity descriptions truncate sooner
1B) Single column at all widths, Notifications then Activity
  ✅ Simplest layout, one reading path, easiest to make accessible and responsive
  ✅ Same priority order on every device, nothing to re-learn between phone and desktop
  ❌ Wastes horizontal space on lg screens; Activity sits below the fold on desktop
1C) Leave the order to the implementer
  ✅ No spec time now, implementer has freedom (human: 0 / CC: 0)
  ✅ Can be tuned later once real data exists
  ❌ Most likely result is three equal-weight panels with no clear first read
Net: a ranked, actionable-first layout versus simplicity or deferral.

options.label: 1A Notifications first (recommended)
options.description: lg: 2 columns, Notifications 7/12 + Activity 5/12; below lg: single column Notifications → Activity.

options.label: 1B Single column always
options.description: Notifications then Activity, one column at every width (max-w ~720px centered).
